messages:
andrea: getting paged — sudden spike in 5xx for /v1/paging/next. started around the v0.16.1 SDK canary ramp at 03:40 UTC. 5xx ~22% of requests in canary cohort.
andrea: sample error patterns: older clients see `422 Unprocessable Entity` when sending cursors; canary clients see streaming timeouts + proxy 504s.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: HIGH - paging-canary-0.16.1 (ID: INC-20260315-02). Paging errors breached SLA thresholds. Pager: @sam.
sam: oncall ack — will triage. @maya can you confirm ff state and canary config?
maya: ff `paging-sdk-v0-16-1` set to gradual ramp starting 03:40 with canary=15%. I see an unintended spike to ~60% because our traffic router applied a staged rollout twice due to a race condition.
maya: flipping ff off now: `ffctl toggle paging-sdk-v0-16-1 off --env prod`
ops-bot: Feature flag `paging-sdk-v0-16-1` toggled OFF by maya at 03:46:08 UTC. Propagation ~20s.
eli: I noticed a related deploy: paging-proxy was updated earlier today with PR #1248 that changed cursor validation to require a hyphenated token. Might be rejecting base64-only cursors.
andrea: customer-ops, list top affected tenants.
customer-ops: pulling logs — top affected: Nimbus Inc, Alder Labs, Streamly. Reaching out. Workaround suggested: pin to SDK 0.15.x or set env var `REDWOOD_PAGING_LEGACY_CURSOR=1`.
david: initial theory: SDK 0.16.1 changed cursor wire format to use dotted tokens and changed streaming init header from `X-Stream-Proto: 1` to `X-Stream-Proto: 2`. The proxy's stricter cursor validation + new router code path cause mixed failures depending on routing path.
sam: rolling back canary group to previous image: `kubectl -n redwood-prod rollout undo deployment/paging-api --to-revision=87` — starting now.
ops-bot: Rollout undo initiated for deployment/paging-api in namespace redwood-prod.
maya: traffic metrics — after ff off and rollback start, 5xx dropped from 22% -> 7% in ~3 minutes.
incident-bot: Severity set to MEDIUM — mitigation in progress.
andrea: assign two parallel follow-ups: 1) quick router permissive-parse hotfix (ENG-PLATFORM-4601) to accept legacy and new cursors for 2 hours; 2) SDK patch to gate handshake header change behind explicit opt-in (SDK-PR-910). Target: hotfix in 90m.
david: I'll take ENG-PLATFORM-4601. Plan: add tolerant cursor parser and a config flag `allow_legacy_cursor=true` defaulted in prod for 24h. Will open PR and request expedited review.
customer-ops: Nimbus replied — they've reverted to 0.15.4 and confirmed services restored. Alder Labs prefers we hold the fix; they want an explicit compatibility doc.
sam: handoff: I'll own immediate stabilization until 04:30 UTC, after that david owns postmortem + fix rollout.
maya: enabling elevated logging on paging route for 1 hour: `logs set-level paging-route DEBUG --window 60m` to capture failures and any router race state.
eli: adding note — the router double-ramp bug was fixed in a separate ticket but not deployed to all regions; coincidence aligned with canary window. Will coordinate regional rollout pause.
andrea: customers updated and workarounds provided. Any sign of regressions from rollback?
maya: no new regressions observed. monitoring shows request latency stable and error delta near baseline.
incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-02 auto-closed at 1784000156 by incident-bot (severity: MEDIUM).
andrea: thanks team. Post-incident action items: ENG-PLATFORM-4601 (router tolerant parser) — david, SDK-PR-910 (opt-in handshake change) — eli, CANARY-GUARD-22 (prevent duplicate ramp) — maya. Postmortem owner: david. ETA postmortem draft: 2026-03-15 11:30 UTC. :white_check_mark:
